# Percy Jackson: concept-art requests

<!-- Generated by design/source/build_requests.py; edit the data there. -->

Concept art for a game of *The Lightning Thief* and the later books, in the chosen direction:
**cartoon heroes in an ornamental world**. The heroes are clean, bright cartoon
characters; the world, maps and interface are flat decorative illustration in
the manner of Greek vases, with black-and-gold frames. See
[the style reference](../reference/README.md), families 5, 6 and 10.

These images are for planning: they set the look of the cast and places
before any game is built. They are not yet game assets.

## How to generate

1. Generate **`key-art` first**. It fixes the look. Attach it as a reference to
   every later request, together with the sheets named in each **References**
   line.
2. Then the character sheets, then the places and situations, then the
   interface.
3. Save each image as `<id>.png` (for example `char-percy.png`) and drop it in
   [`../intake/`](../intake/README.md). On integration it moves to
   `design/concept/` and this document is rebuilt.

### Round 2: the game in 3D

The game is built in the blocky 3D style of Minecraft Dungeons (see
[the game design](game-design.md)). The round-2 sheets are what the blocky
hero and monster models are built from, so generate them in this order:

1. `char-heroes-2` (the new heroes in the cartoon style) and `vox-key` (the 3D
   look; attach it to every later round-2 request).
2. The seven hero sheets, `vox-percy` to `vox-nico`. These come first because
   the hero models are built from them.
3. The monster and character sheets, then the places.
4. The game art (`logo`, `title-bg`, `ui-hero-cards-2`) and the chapter cards
   whenever convenient; the game draws stand-ins until they arrive.

### Round 5: the open world

Camp Half-Blood now sits in a big open world of eight regions. Generate
`vox-ow-map` first (the layout), then the region scenes, the shared kit
(`vox-ow-props`), the people who give side quests and the champions. The
Road West road trip has its own strip map (`vox-rt-map`), towns, roadside
kit and roadblocks. The game draws blocky stand-ins for all of them until
the sheets arrive.

### Round 6: loot

Item icons for the inventory, pickup cards and shop, and a kit of rarity
frames, badges, the loot beam and drachmas (see [the loot design](loot-design.md)).
Each icon sheet is a grid on flat magenta in the order its prompt lists, so the
game can key out the background and cut it into cells. Generate
`icons-weapons-1` first and attach it to the others so the icons match. The
game shows its emoji icons until the sheets arrive.

### Round 7: gear on the heroes

Every weapon a hero equips is drawn in their hand and every armour changes
their outfit (game/js/entities/gear/). The models are procedural stand-ins
until these sheets fix their look: generate `vox-gear-weapons-1` and
`vox-gear-armour-1` first and attach them to the second sheet of each pair.

Concept sheets land in `design/concept/`; files marked as game art land in
`game/assets/`. Drop either kind in the intake folder.

Every prompt includes the shared style and palette, so each can be pasted as it
is. Prompts describe the look rather than naming any artist, and the characters
are original designs drawn from the books, not likenesses of actors.

## Shared style

> Cartoon heroes in an ornamental world: the characters are drawn in a clean, bright cartoon style (ink outlines, flat cel-shaded colour, expressive faces) and stand in front of a world painted as flat decorative illustration: layered patterned shapes, waves, clouds and smoke drawn as curling ornamental ribbons, Greek-key and wave-scroll borders, black-figure and red-figure vase motifs, fine gold-leaf linework on deep teal, navy and black grounds, a subtle paper grain. Modern places (New York, highways, Las Vegas) get the same ornamental treatment, so that skyscrapers and neon look as if painted on an ancient vase. Exciting rather than frightening: monsters are bold and dramatic, never gory. Palette: camp orange #f28c28, sea teal #0f6f73, deep navy #10233d, jade #2e8b6e, coral #e8664a, bronze gold #c9963a, lightning yellow #ffd84a, parchment cream #f4ead5, vase black #17130f and owl grey #8c96a3.

Character sheets use:

> Clean, bright cartoon illustration for a 2D adventure game for players aged 8 to 14: confident ink outlines of varying weight, flat cel-shaded colour with one shadow tone and a small highlight, expressive faces with large readable eyes but natural proportions (the twelve-year-olds about six heads tall), lively poses and strong silhouettes that read at small size. Original character designs, not likenesses of any actor. Palette: camp orange #f28c28, sea teal #0f6f73, deep navy #10233d, jade #2e8b6e, coral #e8664a, bronze gold #c9963a, lightning yellow #ffd84a, parchment cream #f4ead5, vase black #17130f and owl grey #8c96a3.

### Round 7 · Gear on the heroes: weapons in hand, armour worn

#### `vox-gear-weapons-2` — Weapons in hand 2: the legendaries

- **File:** `vox-gear-weapons-2.png`, 2400 × 1600 px, delivered to `design/concept/vox-gear-weapons-2.png`
- **References:** `vox-key`, `vox-percy`, `icons-weapons-2`, `vox-gear-weapons-1`
- **Use:** Fixes the look of the legendary and boss-signature weapon models (game/js/entities/gear/weapons.js).
- **Status:** requested

> A model sheet of blocky 3D voxel weapons, each a separate held model laid out in rows on a flat light-grey background at one shared scale (a hero's fist is one block), seen from the high three-quarter game angle with the grip at the bottom left and the point or head at the top right, as a hero holds it; each weapon readable at small size by its silhouette, with a small second view of its most distinctive part beside it. In this order: 1. Backbiter, a sword whose blade is half celestial bronze and half grey steel, split lengthwise, with a dark spiked crossguard; 2. Stygian Iron Blade, a black sword with a violet glowing edge that drinks the light; 3. Twin Huntress Knives, a pair of curved silver moon-knives; 4. Imperial Gold Gladius, a short Roman sword of shining gold with an eagle-head pommel; 5. Harpe of Perseus, a silver sword with a sickle hook curving off its spine; 6. Club of Heracles, a huge knotty olive-wood club studded with bronze, held in both hands; 7. Pelian Spear of Achilles, a long spear banded in gold with a blue pennant; 8. Burning Sword of Ares, a broad black blade with a red-hot core and flames along its edges; 9. Axe of Boreas, a two-handed ice-blue axe with frost crystals growing from it; 10. Spear of the Storm, a silver spear head wrapped in forked white lightning; 11. Tide-Forged Sword, a sea-green bronze blade with a wave-shaped crossguard and a trident pommel; 12. Fury's Flaming Lash, a leather handle and a coil of fire held out like a whip; 13. Horn of the Minotaur, a great curved bull's horn held by its leather-bound root; 14. Chimera Fang Spear, a spear tipped with a poison-green glowing fang, a lion's mane tassel and a snake tail wound down the shaft; 15. Procrustes's Cleaver, a butcher's cleaver the size of a door with a measuring rule along it, held in both hands. 3D game art in the blocky voxel style of Minecraft Dungeons: characters built from cubes, with a large cube head whose face is simple pixel art (about 8 × 8 pixels: pixel eyes, a pixel mouth, hair drawn as pixels and as a few blocky tufts), a boxy torso, square arms and legs, crisp pixel-art textures (about 16 pixels per block) with simple shading, chunky readable silhouettes; warm cinematic lighting, soft ambient occlusion and glowing magic effects. Costume colours and details follow the Camp Half-Blood cartoon concept art. Palette: camp orange #f28c28, sea teal #0f6f73, deep navy #10233d, jade #2e8b6e, coral #e8664a, bronze gold #c9963a, lightning yellow #ffd84a, parchment cream #f4ead5, vase black #17130f and owl grey #8c96a3. No lettering, logos, captions or watermark.
